classification.difficultyReason: Link the given gradient and point or intercept to a line equation, determine both intercepts, and represent the line graphically with labelled axis intersections.

content.prompt: Draw a graph of the straight line that satisfies the following features. Label any intersections with the coordinate axes where possible.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}y-0&=3(x-6)\\y&=3x-18\end{align*}$$
Plot $(6,0)$ and $(0,-18)$, then draw the straight line through them.

spec.description: Increasing straight line with arrowheads at both ends; only the intercept ticks are numbered. No grid. Source blue series is standardised to booklet blue.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Gradient $2$ and passing through the point $(1,4)$.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}y-4&=2(x-1)\\y-4&=2x-2\\y&=2x+2\\0&=2x+2\\x&=-1\end{align*}$$
Plot $(-1,0)$ and $(0,2)$, then draw the straight line through them. It passes through $(1,4)$.

spec.description: Increasing straight line with arrowheads at both ends; only the intercept ticks are numbered. No grid. Source blue series is standardised to booklet blue.

children.label: d
children.prompt: Gradient $\frac12$ and passing through the point $(-4,1)$.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}y-1&=\frac12(x+4)\\y-1&=\frac12x+2\\y&=\frac12x+3\\0&=\frac12x+3\\x&=-6\end{align*}$$
Plot $(-6,0)$ and $(0,3)$, then draw the straight line through them. It passes through $(-4,1)$.

spec.description: Shallow increasing straight line with arrowheads at both ends; only the intercept ticks are numbered. No grid. Source blue series is standardised to booklet blue.
